title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-ivy-2026-03-04
content:
Back-of-envelope notes: pricing & packaging ideas (scratchpad)

Context / goals:
- Need simple hosted API pricing that:
  - covers unit cost + margins (~60% gross),
  - scales to high-volume customers,
  - gives clear cost signals (batching, caching, quantization).
- Also thinking about how to present Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs hosted API vs Private pricing.

Assumptions (baseline for convos/generation):
- Typical request pattern: prompt 50 tokens in, model generates 150 tokens avg (total 200 tokens per call).
- Average tokens/sec generation (throughput) for production-optimized model on inference instance: 50 tok/sec (conservative for small-medium models), 200 tok/sec for aggressive batching on large cards.
- GPU cost: use blended infra cost for hosted API instances ~ $3.00/hr per effective inference slot (this is after amortization, multi-tenant efficiency).
- Infra+network+storage+ops overhead: add 30% on top of GPU cost.
- SRE/observability + support allocations: add another 10% on top.
- Total markup we need (cost -> price): target gross margin 60% => price = cost / (1 - 0.60) = cost / 0.4 => 2.5x cost.

Key formulae:
- cost_per_second = gpu_cost_per_hour / 3600
- cost_per_token = cost_per_second / tokens_per_second (raw GPU share)
- total_unit_cost_per_token = cost_per_token * (1 + infra_overhead + support_overhead)
- list_price_per_token = total_unit_cost_per_token * (1 / (1 - target_margin))

Compute (baseline numbers):
- gpu_cost_per_hour = $3.00 => cost_per_second = 3 / 3600 = $0.0008333/s
- tokens_per_second = 50 => cost_per_token_raw = 0.0008333 / 50 = $0.000016666 => $0.016666 per 1k tokens
- overheads: infra 30% + support 10% => multiplier = 1.4 => unit_cost_per_token = 0.000016666 * 1.4 = 0.000023333 => $0.023333 per 1k tokens
- target margin 60% => price_per_token = 0.000023333 / 0.4 = 0.000058333 => $0.058333 per 1k tokens

So baseline hosted list price ~ $0.058 per 1k tokens (generation).
Notes: this feels in the ballpark for efficient open models on optimized infra. If GPU cost or perf changes, this moves linearly.

Example customer math (monthly):
- Developer (small): 10M tokens/month => cost to us: 10,000 * 0.023333 = $233.33 => price@list (2.5x) = $583.33 => we collect $583 (gross margin ~60% ~ $350).
- Mid-sized: 200M tokens/month => cost to us = 200k * 0.023333 = $4,666 => price = $11,666. We might offer volume discount 20% => $9,333 final (effective margin a bit lower).

Embedding pricing (different perf/cost):
- Embedding generation is cheaper per token but longer context for some models. Assume embeddings throughput 100 tok/sec and same GPU hourly cost.
- cost_per_token_raw = 0.0008333 / 100 = 0.000008333 => 0.008333 per 1k tokens raw. With overhead 1.4 => 0.011666 per 1k tokens. Price at 60% margin => 0.029166 per 1k tokens => round to $0.03 per 1k tokens for hosted embeddings.
- Alternative: bill embeddings per 1k chars or per vector ~ (simplify): $0.0003 per embed for small vectors => translate when we have vector size data.

Dedicated / Reserved capacity thinking:
- Dedicated contract: customer pays committed $/month for reserved GPU capacity.
- Example: one reserved slot equivalent to n hosted slots; price should be a predictable monthly rate. Use simple formula: committed_price = (expected_util_hours * gpu_hour_cost_on_commit * (1 - commit_discount)) + platform_fee.
- If on-demand hosted list equates to $0.058 per 1k tokens, and a large customer expects 100B tokens/month -> list cost = 100,000k * 0.058 = $5.8M => obviously we give huge discounts and recommend Dedicated with committed infra.
- Quick guess: Dedicated reserved GPU (high throughput) cost to Redwood ~ $6/hr actual (because dedicated hardware + networking + HR + SLA) -> $6 * 24 * 30 = $4,320/mo per GPU. Add 40% overhead => $6,048 cost to us. To get 60% gross, sell at $15k/mo per GPU-ish. This is very rough and needs modeling by infra team.

Pricing tiers (sketch):
- Free tier: 100k tokens/month free (trial) + rate limit, no SLA.
- Pay-as-you-go (Developer): $0.06 / 1k tokens generation, $0.03 / 1k tokens embeddings. No commitment.
- Startup / Growth (prepaid credits): volume discounts: 10% off at $1k+/mo, 20% off at $10k+/mo, custom at $50k+.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: commit to $X/mo get reserved throughput, SLA, private networking. Pricing per GPU slot, starting at $15k/mo (negotiable).
- Burst capacity addon: ability to burst to shared pool at premium for peak traffic (~1.5x list).

Product packaging notes:
- Expose cost controls: batching, caching toggles in Console with estimated per-token savings.
- Show effective per-1k token price in billing dashboard after discounts/credits.
- For Dedicated, show an "equivalent hosted price" to justify commit (i.e., show how many tokens/month before Dedicated becomes cheaper).

Risks / open questions:
- We need actual infra cost: current $3/hr blended is a placeholder. Get infra team numbers: benchmark throughput per model variant (tokens/sec) for supported instance types and amortized infra cost per slot.
- Model mix matters a lot: Llama-2-13b vs 70b vs quantized variants change tokens/sec drastically -> price must vary by model family (we already have model catalog).
- Cold-starts, short requests (<100ms) are inefficient; need to account for per-request overhead charge for tiny calls? Could be messy for small chat apps.
- How to bill for function-calls/structured outputs vs raw tokens? Probably still token-based but consider per-call minimal charge.

TODOs / action items:
- [ ] Ask infra + billing for real blended GPU cost per slot + throughput numbers per model (by 2026-03-09).
- [ ] Run sensitivity analysis with GPU cost $2-$12/hr and tokens/sec 20-300 and produce price bands.
- [ ] Draft a short pricing doc for dev portal with clear examples (free + 3 paid tiers + Dedicated contact sales).
- [ ] Validate embedding pricing vs competitors (Pinecone, OpenAI, Cohere) and decide bill-per-embed vs per-1k-token.

Random thoughts / UX rules of thumb:
- Keep list prices simple and rounded: $0.06/1k, $0.03/1k embeddings. People like simple numbers.
- Use metered + commitment discounts (standard cloud approach).
- For platform adoption, generous free tier + easy upgrade flow matters more than squeezing devs on tiny usage.

Endnotes (quick):
- If we wanted a very conservative public price (to avoid undercharging): round to $0.06/1k generation, $0.03/1k embeddings, Dedicated starting at $15k/mo per GPU-slot.
- Everything above is prelim; needs refinement with infra actuals and model perf.
